questions.question: Which of the following can be graph of a function?
questions.explanation:
Let y=f(x) be a graph . So if we draw any possible line parallel to y-axis and that line cut the graph y=f(x) at two or more than two points. Then y=f(x) will not be a function.

Hence the graphs in option (A) and option (B) can not be the graph of a function.

Hence , options (C) and (D) are correct .

questions.question: Let \( A=\{n, i, t\} \) and \( B=\{c, b, s, e\} \). Then which of the following is NOT a function?
questions.explanation:
A function is a relation in which each input is assigned to exactly one output. The set of all possible inputs is called the domain of

the function and the set of all possible outputs is called the range.

Given, A={n,i,t} and

B={c,b,s,e}

Then, {(n,c),(i,b),(t,s)},{(n,b),(i,s),(t,e)} and {(n,b),(i,c),(t,e)} is a function from A to B.

Because every input has exactly one output.

But, {(n,b),(n,s),(t,e)} is not a function from A to B.

Because input n has exactly two output.

Therefore, if A={n,i,t} and B={c,b,s,e}, then {(n,b),(n,s),(t,e)} is not a function from A to B.

questions.question: The domain of the function \( f(x)=\sqrt{x-x^{2}}+\sqrt{4+x}+\sqrt{4-x} \) is:
questions.explanation:
Given the function is, f(x)=x-x2+4+x+4-x

We know that, the square root function is defined in real if the under root function is greater or equal to zero. 

So, x-x2≥0

⇒x(1-x)≥0

Since if the product of two number is positive then either both are positive or both negative,

Either,  x≤0 and 1-x≤0⇒x≥1, It is not possible. 

Or, x≥0 and 1-x≥0⇒x≤1

Hence, 0≤x≤1....(i)

Again, 4+x≥0

x≥-4....(ii)

And 4-x≥0

x≤4...(iii)

Comparing (i),(ii) we get, 

-4≤x,0≤x⇒0≤x....(iv)

Comparing (i),(iii) we get, 

x≤1,x≤4⇒x≤1....(v)

Combining (iv),(v) we get, 

0≤x≤1⇒x∈[0,1]

Thus the domain of the function is [0,1].

Hence the correct option is (D).
